name: Hidden-value equality across credentials

request.issue: cred-spec #9 (geoffturk 2026-09-10, point 4: 'a child's issuer MUST equal its parent's subject, so proving chain validity without disclosing the chain is hidden-value equality across credentials signed by different parties. No holder secret is involved … name the chain predicates separately so they do not appear covered while having no stated primitive') · cred-spec §Zero-Knowledge and Selective Disclosure editor's note (merged 2026-09-10): the VDC chain, the VAC chain and 'two credentials presented together share a subject' listed as predicates waiting on the ZKP task force
request.by: geoffturk / stormer78 (cred-spec #9; §Zero-Knowledge and Selective Disclosure editor's note) — specified by the ZKP TF co-chair
request.need: three credential-layer predicates need a proof that a hidden value in one signed credential equals a hidden value in another signed credential — a child hop's `issuer` and its parent's `credentialSubject.id`; the subject of a VMC and the subject of a VAC presented together — with no holder secret in the relation, so record 007 does not apply and nothing else names it

statement: A verifier learns that a hidden field of one authenticated credential equals a hidden field of another authenticated credential — the two signed by different parties — without learning the value, and without the proof introducing a value that correlates across presentations.
witness: the two credentials (their bytes stay with the holder) and the openings of the two committed fields being compared

the issuer signatures or the leaf commitments that authenticate each credential's content — whichever the enclosing record binds (the equality clause on its own compares two witnesses; the enclosing record's signature-verify or set-membership clauses are what make them authenticated)
publicInputs: whatever the enclosing record discloses of the two credentials — this record adds no public input of its own
transcriptDigest — the presentation transcript this proof is bound to; the binding is record 003's clause, which the enclosing record carries (does-not-establish)

relation.clause: field_a (opened from credential A's authenticated content) equals field_b (opened from credential B's authenticated content), each taken whole in the profile's canonical form and injective encoding (issuance): field_a − field_b = 0 on every element of the encoding — a differing pair is unsatisfiable, and neither value is a public signal

disclosureSet: nothing about the value: no digest, commitment or pseudonym derived from it leaves the proof — the enclosing record decides what else is shown
doesNotEstablish: common control: equal identifiers in two credentials say that the same DID appears in both, not that the presenter controls it — key control is record 004, and two different identifiers under one hand is record 007

that either credential is authentic, valid or unrevoked on its own — the enclosing record's signature-verify (or set-membership) and non-revocation clauses establish that; this clause compares two witnesses those clauses have already bound
that the two credentials were meant to be presented together — intentional correlation is the holder's declaration (record 012), and a shared subject widens no identifier's declared scope

anything about the value's meaning: an equal `issuer` and `credentialSubject.id` across two hops establishes the link the chain rule requires (cred-spec §Delegation Edges, §Attenuation) and nothing about who that party is

that the proof is bound to its transcript by this clause alone: transcriptDigest is a public input the hidden-equality clause does not read, and in Groth16 a public input that appears in no constraint can be replaced after proving. The binding is record 003's clause — the circuit constrains the scalar — carried by the enclosing record, or composed with this one where it is proven on its own; a circuit for this record that leaves the input unconstrained does not conform

authenticity of a credential whose `issuer` is hidden, under the as-signed option: hiding the issuer hides the key its signature verifies under, so the enclosing record must verify the signature under a hidden key and show that the key is that identifier's — and no DID is resolved inside a circuit (Integration). Three shapes meet this: a self-certifying identifier (`did:key`, `did:peer` numalgo 0) whose key is decoded from the hidden identifier inside the proof; a committed identifier-to-key binding the proof opens (a registry leaf under a public root, or a key commitment the parent credential carries for its subject); or an issuer-hiding signature scheme. None is selected: it is an open requirement of records 020 and 021

adversary.claim: the compared value is not disclosed and no value derived from it is emitted; two verifiers comparing proofs learn only what the enclosing records disclosed to each

the proof emits no value by which the issuer of either credential can recognise it: the equality is proven over openings the holder supplies, never over a public signal. What an issuer already holds is outside the claim — the parent's issuer wrote the parent's `credentialSubject.id`, which is the compared value, so where the enclosing record's disclosures let that issuer recognise its credential it learns that the other credential names the same identifier

horizon: the shorter of the two credentials' validity periods — the equality is a statement about two credentials as issued, and a re-issued credential must be re-compared
the hash/commitment cryptoperiod of the leaf or field commitments the openings are made against

forgery: none inside the relation under the Poseidon-openings option; the as-signed option inherits ECDSA / Ed25519 — the compared fields are authenticated by signatures that become forgeable

rejectionCodes: hidden-values-differ (unsat: the two openings are not equal)
field-not-openable (verify-fail: a compared field carries no commitment the proof can open — an issuance failure, X3 applied to the compared fields)
encoding-not-injective (lint: the profile compares a truncated or length-free packing of the identifier)

options.construction: Groth16/Poseidon: two Poseidon openings of the compared fields (the circom-gadget leaf commitment, twice) plus one equality constraint — conjecture: the openings are the whole cost, the equality is one constraint
options.cost: unmeasured (conjecture ≈ 2 × the lab's Poseidon leaf commitment + 1; one compile settles it)
options.source: runtimes/circom-gadget (Poseidon commitment already binds a leaf to hidden content)

options.construction: as-signed credentials (ECDSA/Ed25519 rails): equality of two signed fields inside a Longfellow-class or ProveKit circuit — the signature checks are the cost, the equality is free
options.cost: unmeasured; two in-circuit signature verifications at the least. Where either `issuer` is hidden the verification is under a hidden key, with a proof that the key is the hidden identifier's — the larger cost, and not specified (does-not-establish)

options.construction: no proof — the shared value is disclosed and compared in the clear (the credential specification's stated fallback: 'every requirement here can be checked by presenting the credentials themselves … the cost is privacy rather than correctness')
options.cost: zero constraints; the cost is the disclosure of the whole chain or both subjects
options.source: cred-spec §Zero-Knowledge and Selective Disclosure editor's note, 'What holds until this work lands'

issuance: each field that may be compared must be, or carry, a ZK-openable commitment inside the authenticated credential content: for the chain predicates that is `issuer` and `credentialSubject.id` on every hop; for the shared-subject rule it is `credentialSubject.id` on the VMC and the VAC — the X3 requirement applied to the compared fields rather than to signatures (cred-spec #17)

a credential whose compared field is a `pairwise` identifier that differs from the identifier in the other credential cannot satisfy this record by construction; the holder either declared one `directed` identifier for both, or the enclosing record composes record 007 for that pair instead

encoding: a DID is longer than one field element (about 31 bytes on BN254 or BLS12-381), so the compared value is never a truncation. The profile fixes one of two encodings — an injective packing (the UTF-8 bytes in 31-byte limbs with the byte length as a further element, compared element by element), or a domain-separated collision-resistant hash of the whole string to one field element, where equality then rests on that hash. A truncated or length-free packing accepts unequal identifiers, which is a soundness failure

normalisation: both fields are reduced to one canonical form before encoding — an `issuer` given as an object is read as its `id`; a DID is compared without fragment, query or path; no case folding beyond what the DID method defines — or one identifier written two ways fails to match. The canonical form is the credential specification's to state, as the comparison it already makes in the clear; the proof needs it to be one function of the credential bytes, the same in both credentials

theorems.name: sub_zero_iff_eq
theorems.proves: a − b = 0 exactly when a = b in Fin n, any n > 0 — the constraint is equality, both ways, without primality

hypotheses.name: authenticated openings
hypotheses.carries: the compared fields are the openings the enclosing record's signature-verify or membership clauses bind — carried by the enclosing record

formal.scope: the equality clause alone; common control, authenticity, intent and meaning (does-not-establish 1–4) are out of scope by construction — the clause compares two witnesses
